summary: CREWGUARD SENTINEL is an offline-first astronaut health evidence and decision-support prototype for long-duration space missions. An unusual health measurement does not explain whether the information is incomplete, related to recent activity, affected by environmental context, or different from the astronaut’s personal pattern. CREWGUARD processes structured health information through four stages: TRUST evaluates quality and completeness, PERSONALIZE compares usable information with an illustrative individual profile, INTERPRET examines competing explanations and missing evidence, and ACT ranks the next information to collect and produces an auditable evidence report. The project also includes a separate explorer for NASA OSDR-575 historical Inspiration4 serum research. CREWGUARD does not diagnose, prescribe treatment, or replace a flight surgeon.
details:
CREWGUARD SENTINEL

CREWGUARD SENTINEL is an offline-first astronaut health evidence and decision-support prototype designed for long-duration missions where communication with Earth may be delayed.

The problem

An unusual health value does not explain itself. A measurement may be incomplete, affected by supplied quality information, associated with recent exercise, influenced by missing environmental context, or different from an individual’s usual pattern. Astronauts need a transparent way to evaluate the available evidence without assuming that every unusual value represents a medical condition.

The solution

CREWGUARD processes structured health information through four connected modules:

1. TRUST

TRUST examines the source, completeness, timestamps, missing samples, supplied movement or quality metadata, and other available integrity information. Incomplete or low-quality information is downgraded or blocked from personal-profile updates.

2. PERSONALIZE

PERSONALIZE selects an illustrative Rest, Recovery, or Movement profile and compares the current measurement with that context. The prototype uses the median and Median Absolute Deviation to provide a robust comparison. Synthetic or unreliable information cannot update the profile.

3. INTERPRET

INTERPRET evaluates five possible explanations:

  • measurement-quality limitations,
  • activity or recovery context,
  • environmental or operational context,
  • persistent deviation from the illustrative personal profile,
  • and sleep or fatigue context.

The system may mark an explanation as supported, not indicated, unresolved, or not assessable. It does not force a conclusion when evidence is missing.

4. ACT

ACT assigns transparent evidence-priority points to possible next measurements, such as repeating heart rate, retrieving cabin CO₂, confirming exercise timing, or completing sleep information. Evidence priority represents which input is most likely to reduce uncertainty in the prototype. It is not a medical urgency or severity score.

Counterfactual reasoning

CREWGUARD can hold a synthetic health reading constant while changing contextual information. For example, the same 106-BPM value may be compared with a Recovery profile when exercise occurred recently, or with a Rest profile when exercise occurred much earlier. This demonstrates that the measurement remains unchanged while the evidence interpretation changes.

The system does not claim that sleep, exercise, environmental context, or another factor caused the reading.

NASA resources

CREWGUARD uses NASA resources at two levels.

The NASA Human Research Program provides background on major human-spaceflight hazards, relevant health indicators, mission autonomy, and the need for evidence during communication delay.

The application also includes a research explorer for NASA Open Science Data Repository study OSD-575, Version 3: “SpaceX Inspiration4 Blood Serum Metabolic Panel and Immune/Cardiac Cytokine Arrays.”

The bundled comprehensive metabolic-panel extract contains:

  • 28 science records,
  • 58 columns,
  • four anonymized crew identifiers,
  • seven preflight and postflight timepoints,
  • and nineteen numeric laboratory-measurement fields.

The application allows users to select a crew identifier and laboratory measurement, visualize values across study timepoints, and inspect source records.

NASA historical research remains separate from the synthetic crew-health scenarios. OSD-575 is serum laboratory research, not live telemetry or wearable heart-rate data. The project does not use the study to create personal profiles, define medical thresholds, diagnose a condition, or prescribe treatment.

Inputs

The prototype supports:

  • built-in synthetic demonstration scenarios,
  • manual health check-in,
  • sleep duration,
  • exercise timing,
  • cabin CO₂ context,
  • body temperature,
  • optional blood pressure,
  • glucose,
  • mood,
  • fatigue,
  • and notes.

Sleep duration, exercise timing, and cabin CO₂ affect the reasoning demonstration. Other check-in values are recorded locally but are not assigned unvalidated medical interpretation rules.

Outputs

CREWGUARD produces:

  • a quality and completeness status,
  • an illustrative personal-profile comparison,
  • competing explanations,
  • missing-evidence identification,
  • a ranked next-measurement list,
  • a machine-readable JSON evidence packet,
  • a one-page human-readable report,
  • and a local offline evidence queue.

The offline queue is a browser demonstration and does not communicate with Mission Control.

Technology

The prototype uses:

  • HTML
  • CSS
  • JavaScript
  • Canvas
  • CSV
  • JSON
  • browser localStorage
  • a service worker
  • Python utilities
  • Node.js tests
  • Playwright and Chromium browser testing
  • GitHub
  • GitHub Actions
  • GitHub Pages

The current version is a static application and does not require a backend database, cloud subscription, API key, or login.

Validation

The project’s recorded automated tests report:

  • 17 of 17 unit tests passed
  • 15 of 15 browser checks passed
  • successful GitHub Pages deployment

Testing covers CSV parsing, missing values, quality rules, profile protection, recovery context, persistent-deviation scenarios, NASA research separation, counterfactual reasoning, next-measurement ranking, evidence export, report generation, and mobile layout.

These tests verify prototype software behavior. They do not establish clinical effectiveness, medical-device safety, sensor accuracy, or readiness for actual spaceflight use.

Safety and limitations

CREWGUARD is a competition decision-support prototype.

It:

  • does not diagnose health conditions,
  • does not prescribe medication,
  • does not generate treatment,
  • does not replace a flight surgeon,
  • does not contain real astronaut health records,
  • does not currently connect to physical sensors,
  • does not communicate with Mission Control,
  • and is not clinically validated.

The public demonstration should use only synthetic information because browser localStorage is not encrypted.

Public links

Application:
https://wael-sktch.github.io/crewguard-sentinel/

Source code:
https://github.com/wael-sktch/crewguard-sentinel

Intended impact

CREWGUARD aims to make health-information quality, personal context, uncertainty, research applicability, and the next evidence step easier to understand when immediate support from Earth may be delayed
